title: Live since Oct 11, 2,077 trades, 98.46% win rate. Here's the honest version of how it works.
author: Ok_Security_1684
selftext:
Before the comments fill up with "98% win rate, ok scam": I get it. If I saw that number on someone else's post I'd assume the same thing. So let me deal with it up front instead of pretending it's not the first thing you're thinking.

**I hope some of this ends up being useful for your own systems too, even if it's just one or two ideas you can borrow.**

This is real money on Binance USDT-M futures. Live since Oct 11 2025. Not a backtest, not paper trading, not a screenshot from a strategy that has never paid funding, eaten slippage, or had a fill go the wrong way. 

Now the win rate, because it's the wrong thing to be impressed by. A 98% win rate on its own means almost nothing, and if anything it should make you more suspicious, not less. Any bot that takes small fixed take profits and refuses to close its losers can show 99% wins for months, right up until the day it gives it all back at once. So I'm not posting this as a win rate flex. The number that actually matters is whether the account is still alive and the drawdown is still small. Anyone can win a lot of trades. Surviving without getting liquidated is the hard part, and that's the part I built the system around.

Performance:

Total PnL: +23,191.11 USDT (+67.09%)

Win rate: 98.46% (2,045 of 2,077)

Profit factor: 7.77

Max drawdown: 890.20 USDT (2.31%)

How it actually works, three layers, in the order that matters:

The risk engine. This is the real reason the account is still here, and it's the part I've spent about 2.5 years optimizing, far longer than the model. It runs in hedge mode with auto trimming. When a position stays open longer than its expected window, the system opens hedges in the opposite direction off separate, independently validated signals, then uses the realized profit from those hedges to cancel out the unrealized loss on the original position. So I'm not forced into bad stop outs, and I can pull risk down without closing the original trade too early. The drawdown control is what keeps the whole thing sustainable. Everything else is secondary to this.

The LSTM. Direction comes from an LSTM trained on multi timeframe data. It gives me a probabilistic read on where price is likely to go next. By itself it's not enough and I don't let it trade alone, because raw model output gets noisy in ranging markets and that's exactly where bots bleed out. The LSTM is one input, not the trigger.

The confirmation layer. This is what decides whether a trade opens at all. The LSTM's read has to agree with trend alignment across timeframes, momentum, a volatility filter, and a structure check. If even one of them disagrees, nothing fires. I'd rather skip 50 mediocre setups than force one bad one. The result is picky, high frequency scalping, lots of small hit and run trades, and the realized profit stacks up over time instead of riding on any single position.

The part nobody likes to say out loud: this hedge and neutralize approach is not free money, and anyone who tells you otherwise is selling something. The thing that kills a system like this is a strong, sustained one direction trend that outruns the hedges. That's the scenario that can turn a clean 2.3% drawdown into a real problem. I know exactly where that risk lives, so margin stays fixed, no martingale, no averaging into losers, and I watch how open positions correlate with each other, since correlation was the one thing that bit me early on. The drawdown number isn't a trophy. It's the thing I'm actively defending every day.

Happy to go deeper on the confirmation logic or the hedge neutralization mechanics if anyone wants to get into it. You can also DM me to reach it as a bot service.
